exposure: type of birth setting (community vs. hospital)
cohort: The study included 707 individuals from 46 states and the District of Columbia who gave birth during the COVID-19 pandemic from March 1, 2020, to November 1, 2020.
finding: During the COVID-19 pandemic, childbearing people desired community birth options, access to midwives, birth advocates, and transparent communication for a positive experience; midwife care and community birth were associated with higher satisfaction and feeling better informed, while BIPOC individuals reported less satisfaction and more stress.
